name: Mezze
comment: TextMate grammar for VS Code — a mirror of the tree-sitter grammar's TOKEN rules (keywords, operators, literals, comments), plus the four identifier POSITIONS a regex can recognise without parsing: a `let` name, a module qualifier before/after `::`, a `.member`, and a record field before `=`. Those four used to be left out on the grounds that LSP semantic tokens supply them, but collectSemanticTokens opens with `state.parsedModule ?: return emptyList()` — a file that does not parse gets NO semantic tokens, which is the state a file is in while you type it, and it only covers top-level lets besides. Markdown ```mezze fences and any LSP-less consumer get this file alone. What stays out is declaration STRUCTURE: nothing here spans a declaration, because a rule that swallows more than it colors is what made `pub` bleed into the following keyword. The two multi-token rules that remain (#binding, and #keywords' isolated `pub`) are pinned by test/tmgrammar.test.js — add a case there before adding a rule here. Native editors (Zed/nvim/Helix) use the tree-sitter grammar directly.

patterns.comment: Doc comment: `## text`. `##` must be followed by a space/tab or EOL (parser rule).
patterns.name: comment.block.documentation.mezze

patterns.comment: Line comment: `# text`. `#` must be followed by a space/tab or EOL; `#foo`/`#{` are NOT comments.
patterns.name: comment.line.number-sign.mezze

metadata.comment: Compiler metadata `#{ key: value, … }` — an attribute, not a comment. Single-line.
metadata.name: meta.attribute.mezze

patterns.comment: String interpolation `$( expr )` — highlight the inner tokens as real code. `contentName: meta.embedded` scopes the body so themes stop painting it with the enclosing string foreground (that's why `{}` looked like a string). Nested `(...)` are consumed by #balanced-parens so the region ends on the MATCHING `)`, not the first one.

balanced-parens.comment: A parenthesized group `( … )` — used INSIDE string interpolation so a nested `)` doesn't prematurely end the `$( … )` region. Recursively consumes its own nested groups and highlights the inner tokens as code.

patterns.comment: Float: `3.14` (a digit must follow the dot).
patterns.name: constant.numeric.float.mezze

patterns.comment: Visibility modifier — ISOLATED. It must never merge with the following keyword (the entire fix for the old broken-cascade bug). A lone `\b(pub)\b` matches just `pub`, so `pub let` colors `pub` then `let` independently.
patterns.name: storage.modifier.mezze

patterns.comment: All other keywords share one scope (like the tree-sitter @keyword).
patterns.name: keyword.control.mezze

binding.comment: The name a `let` introduces. Listed BEFORE #keywords: both rules start matching at the same `let`, and TextMate breaks an index tie by list order. A bare `let` with no name yet — the state you are in while typing — matches neither capture here and falls through to #keywords, so the keyword never loses its color. A regex cannot tell a function from a value, so both get entity.name.function, the same call website/src/lib/highlight.ts makes for its tk-fn.

type-variable.comment: Type variable `'a` — a leading apostrophe. Colored distinctly from concrete types (which the LSP colors as @type).
type-variable.name: variable.parameter.type.mezze

namespace.comment: A module path segment: the lower identifier on either side of `::`. Both sides, so `use std::codec::json` tags all three — the trailing segment is the module being imported, and tree-sitter's (module_path (lower_identifier)) @namespace covers it too. Uppercase names are left to #constructor, so `codec::Entry` colors the qualifier and the type differently.
namespace.name: entity.name.namespace.mezze

constructor.comment: An Upper-cased identifier is a variant constructor / type / effect / ability name at the token level. Which of those it is depends on context — the LSP refines it via semantic tokens; here we give it the type/constructor tint as a reasonable base.
constructor.name: entity.name.type.mezze

patterns.comment: A method CALL — `.name` applied to arguments, which in Mezze means a following `{` or `(`. Splitting on that lookahead is how one regex reproduces tree-sitter's two captures, @function.method for method_call and @variable.member for member_access. Requiring a lowercase letter after the dot also keeps `UserId.(5)` intact: newtype construction is `.(`, not a member.
patterns.name: entity.name.function.member.mezze

patterns.comment: Field access. The `(?<!\.)` guard is load-bearing: without it the third dot of a spread matches and `[...ys]` renders as if `ys` were a member of something. A spread is not an access. The website highlighter had exactly this bug.
patterns.name: variable.other.property.mezze

record-field.comment: A record field name: `{ a = 1 }`. The `[^=]` keeps `==` out. A `let` binding cannot reach here — #binding matches from the earlier `let`, and TextMate takes the leftmost match.
record-field.name: variable.other.property.mezze
